run.finalText:
Checking why the line shows fully at 0.5s, since the trim keys look right.
The reveal is built and runs 7s on the near-black (#0a0908) 1080×1920 canvas. I checked it on a contact sheet at six points, not by playing it through.

- **Gold line:** a 2px champagne line (#d4b886) draws slowly from top to bottom between 0.5s and 4.5s, with a gentle ease in and out.
- **ÉCLAT:** a wide-tracked light serif in champagne gold. The letters fade in one at a time from 2.2s, about 0.45s apart, each with a soft fade. It sits in the lower middle, with a lot of empty space around it.
- **Tracking:** letter-spacing can't be keyframed here. Instead the title scales from 105% to 100% over 2.2–6.8s, which gives a subtle sense of the tracking tightening.
- **EAU DE PARFUM:** a small tracked subtitle in a dimmer gold that fades in at 4.6–6.2s, after the name has settled.

The line is a thin rectangle that grows, not a path with a trim, because the path trim didn't render in the preview. It looks the same on screen.

The title may sit a few pixels right of centre, because the trailing letter-spacing adds space after the last letter. I haven't checked this closely, and I can nudge it if you want.

I can slow the letter stagger further, add a faint gold glow behind the name, or add a short horizontal line under the subtitle.
